title: Ripple
intro: Ping the maze. [b]scan()[/b] floods outward from the exit, one ring at a time, and writes each tile's distance on the floor. Then walk downhill: [b]closer_ahead()[/b] is true when that step brings you one tile nearer.
cs_note: [b]Breadth-first search[/b] uses a queue (first in, first out), so it labels tiles in order of distance. Walking downhill on those numbers follows a shortest path: the same "flow field" trick that steers crowds of enemies in strategy games.
hints: scan() first, then loop until you're at the exit.
If closer_ahead(): move; elif closer_left(): turn left; else: turn right.

scan() writes every tile's distance to the exit on the floor. Then only walk downhill: if the tile ahead is closer, move(); otherwise turn left if that side is closer, or else turn right. Every move takes you one step nearer, so you follow a shortest path. Put scan() above the while, not inside it: one scan is enough, and each costs 5 stamina.
